title: Validating the use of large language models for psychological text classification

paper.authors: Hannah L. Bunt, A. Goddard, Tom W. Reader, Alex Gillespie (LSE)
paper.venue: Frontiers in Social Psychology 3:1460277 (published 2025-02-21, CC BY); funded by SNSF 51NF40-205605
paper.note: No code repository; prompts and codebooks are in the Frontiers Supplementary Material (https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/frsps.2025.1460277/full#supplementary-material). The OSF links in the scaffold (osf.io/h2b8t, osf.io/sekf5) are cited preprints, not artifacts.

dependence.note: GPT-4o is validated as a zero-shot coder of three psychological constructs against human gold-standard coding (N = 1,500 per dataset; 1/3 development, 2/3 held-out test). The paper's contribution is the validity of the LLM classifier itself (tool validity).

claim.statement: Zero-shot gpt-4o-2024-05-13 with iteratively developed prompts reproduces human coding on the held-out test sets (n = 1,000 per dataset): reported speech in online diaries - MaxFew prompt weighted F1 = 0.91 (precision 0.85, recall 0.77); other-initiations of repair in Reddit dialogues - MinZero F1 = 0.91 (precision 0.72, recall 0.84; MaxFew also 0.91); ordinal harm in NHS healthcare complaints - MinZero weighted kappa = 0.57 with exact agreement 0.34 (Table 4, 'Confirmatory predictive validity').
claim.metric: precision and recall of positive cases and weighted F1 (binary tasks); exact agreement and weighted kappa (ordinal harm) between LLM labels and human gold labels on the test split
claim.original_source: Table 4 (test split) and Table 2 (development split), Table 1 (datasets) of the Frontiers article

protocol.model_status: dying, OpenAI shutdown 2026-10-23 (target_models.json). gpt-4-turbo (also in the scaffold's live list) was used only in pilot testing 'to a limited extent' (Limitations) and is NOT an experimental arm - the live arm is gpt-4o-2024-05-13.
protocol.endpoint: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions (Python pipeline iterating over single units of analysis; no conversation memory)
protocol.prompt_source: Supplementary Material of the article (final prompts for the three tasks, three variants each: MinZero = minimal definition zero-shot, MaxZero = maximal definition zero-shot, MaxFew = maximal definition few-shot; plus codebooks incl. the HCAT harm manual) - not downloaded; not in a repo

messages.content: <research-assistant persona for the classification task> (exact text in the Supplementary Material)

<task definition (+ examples for MaxFew) + unit of analysis: diary paragraph / Reddit post-comment pair / healthcare complaint> -> structured label (span + binary; binary; ordinal harm with reasoning)

params.other: zero-shot, no fine-tuning; each unit coded independently

protocol.n_items: 3 datasets x 1,500 units (500 development + 1,000 test each): diaries (10 diaries, 1,500 paragraphs), Reddit (387 dialogues from 27 subreddits, 1,500 posts/comments), NHS complaints (1,500 OCR-processed documents, coded per Gillespie & Reader 2016)
protocol.evaluation: Automatic given the human gold labels: precision/recall/weighted F1 (binary), exact agreement + weighted kappa (ordinal); the paper notes run-to-run variation even at temperature 0 (Section 5.2.4), so report per-seed values.
protocol.environment_check: None possible without the data; if data are obtained, re-score the authors' archived LLM labels (if provided) against gold before new calls.

artifacts.prompts_path: Frontiers Supplementary Material (prompts + codebooks; file names not enumerated by our fetch)
artifacts.data_license: restricted: datasets contain private/sensitive information; access requests to h.l.bunt@lse.ac.uk
artifacts.notes: Reddit data are also subject to platform terms; NHS complaints are confidential documents.

no code released; the pipeline must be rebuilt from the description

budget.assumptions: test split only: 3 datasets x 1,000 units x 3 prompt variants = 9,000 calls per seed x 3 seeds; ~900 input tokens on average (MaxFew prompts with examples and long complaints push this up), ~60 output tokens. Core claim only (best prompt per dataset): 3,000 calls per seed, ~$49 for 3 seeds.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 on Table 4: survival if reported-speech and OIR weighted F1 stay >= 0.85 (within the original's bootstrap 95% CI over test items around 0.91) and harm weighted kappa stays in the 'moderate' band (0.4-0.6); partial if F1 falls to 0.75-0.85 or kappa to 0.2-0.4; death if F1 < 0.75 or kappa < 0.2 (tool no longer valid).
judgment.notes: Successor arms must use the same prompts unchanged; prompt re-development would test a different tool.

user_checks: Request data access from the corresponding author (h.l.bunt@lse.ac.uk) - are we willing to sign a data-use agreement for the diary/Reddit/NHS datasets?
Confirm the live arm is gpt-4o-2024-05-13 (not gpt-4-turbo, which was only piloted).
Download the Frontiers Supplementary Material and verify that the three prompt variants per task are given verbatim.
domain_notes: A validity-methodology paper for psychologists: the two-stage development/test split guards against prompt overfitting, and human inter-rater reliability was itself moderate for reported speech (alpha = 0.66). Weighted F1 on imbalanced binary data (24% positives) is inflated by correct negatives - precision/recall of positives are the informative numbers. The harm task (HCAT ordinal severity) is where GPT-4o systematically over-coded harm; kappa = 0.57 is the fragile quantity.
